newsitem.title: USA: Daschle says prospects for expanding NAFTA poor.
newsitem.headline: Daschle says prospects for expanding NAFTA poor.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Thomas Daschle said Tuesday that prospects for extending the North American Free Trade Agreement to Chile were "not very good."

After addressing the executive council of the AFL-CIO, Daschle told reporters that before Chile could be considered as new member of NAFTA, Congress would have to take a "very careful look" at how the treaty has worked so far.
"I would say the prospects for extending NAFTA to Chile are not very good," Daschle said.
House Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt told reporters that he believed NAFTA was not helping workers.

"In a way NAFTA has validated a system, a governmental and business system (in Mexico), that does not allow workers to have the ability to get paid and compensated for their hard work," Gephardt said.

"If we're going to have fast track then there has to be confidence that it will bring back treaties that improve on the provisions in NAFTA and put those provisions in the core treaty, not in side treaties," Gephardt said.

Gephardt was referring to side agreements with Mexico covering labor and environment issues. The Clinton administration has been pushing to get the broadest possible authority to negotiate labor and environmental issues. But Republicans who control Congress oppose providing "fast track" trade negotiation authority that includes authority to negotiate labor and environmental issues.
The remarks by Gephardt and Daschle underscore the difficulty President Clinton faces in winning support from his own Democrats without the labor and environment provisions.
Fast track would allow the administration to negotiate an expansion of NAFTA to include Chile without fear the agreement will be later changed by Congress.
